body_md: URL shortener: need 100M URLs/month, 10:1 reads. API POST /shorten, GET /:code. Store mapping in KV, cache hot in Redis. Bottleneck is write hotspot; snippet hashes with base62.
output:
code = 7-char md5 hex, e.g. '5d41402'
// base62 in prod; KV write + Redis for hot codes; POST -> 201 + Location

quiz.explain: Hash plus dedupe plus cache handles read-heavy load.
options: Store full URLs in SQL and join on each lookup
Base62 codes in a KV store, hot codes cached
Use the full SHA-256 hash as the short code
Redirect by scanning a table for the long URL
quiz.q: What's the core trick in a URL shortener?

body_md: Twitter feed: requirements fan-out 300M users, timeline <200ms. API post, follow, timeline. Storage posts in Cassandra, graph in social DB. Bottleneck celebrity fan-out; snippet pushes async.
code:
// on post: for follower in followers[author]
//   feed_cache.lpush(follower, post_id)
hook: News feed fan-out: push, pull, and the celebrity problem.
output:
post_id appended to each follower's cached timeline
// celebrity path: skip push, followers pull at read

options: Push every post into every follower's timeline
Pull and merge all followees on each read
Store all timelines in one sharded SQL table
Push for most users, pull for celebrity posts
quiz.q: How do you scale feed fan-out?

takeaway: Push normal, pull celebrities, cache timelines.
trap: Pure pull scanning 1000 follows per read.

body_md: Rate limiter: need 10k rps API protection, burst 50. API gateway check. Storage Redis buckets per key with Lua. Bottleneck central Redis; snippet uses token bucket Lua.
code:
-- lua: refill then allow
local t = redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) or 0
hook: Distributed rate limiter: flood control at 10k rps.
output:
t = current count or 0; refill by elapsed, allow if tokens suffice
// Lua runs atomically: global rate holds across nodes

quiz.explain: Atomic Lua on Redis enforces global rate.
options: In-memory counters on each separate API instance
In the client SDK, trusting it to self-limit
Shared Redis buckets updated by atomic Lua
A SQL row per key, read then updated in two steps
quiz.q: Where does distributed rate limiting live?

body_md: Chat: need 1M concurrent WebSockets, <100ms delivery, presence. API WS connect, send, presence heartbeat. Storage messages in Cassandra, presence in Redis. Bottleneck conn fan-out; snippet uses pub/sub.
hook: Chat at scale: a million sockets and who is online.
output:
msg published to room:<room>; each gateway delivers locally
// <100ms fan-out; presence via heartbeat

quiz.explain: Sticky gateway plus pub/sub reaches all holders.
options: Clients poll for new messages every second
One big server holding every socket in memory
WebSocket gateways joined by pub/sub fan-out
Store presence in Postgres, updated per heartbeat

trap: No resume token losing messages on reconnect.

body_md: S3 object store: need 11 nines, multipart uploads, presigned URLs. API PUT /object, GET range. Storage erasure-coded chunks plus metadata DB. Bottleneck metadata; snippet signs URL.
hook: Object storage like S3: blobs at exabyte scale.
output:
url = 'https://b.s3.../k?X-Amz-Signature=...'
// client PUTs bytes direct; app tier bypassed

options: Stream every upload byte through the app servers
Base64 the file into a JSON API request
Presigned URLs for direct-to-storage uploads
Write each object to one big replicated disk

takeaway: Sign URLs, store chunks with metadata index.

body_md: Pastebin variant: requirements 10M pastes/month, TTL, burn-after-read. API POST paste, GET raw. Storage object store plus metadata Postgres. Bottleneck spam; snippet expires keys.
hook: Pastebin design: text hosting with self-destruct.
output:
OK (TTL 86400); GETDEL returns value once, then nil
// expiry + burn-after-read contain spam

quiz.explain: TTL plus optional one-time read contains abuse.
options: Keep every paste forever in Postgres rows
Sequential IDs so pastes are easy to share
Default TTL plus optional burn-after-read
Hold all pastes in app server memory for speed
quiz.q: What's the key design idea for a pastebin?

takeaway: Expire by default, burn on demand.

body_md: Search autocomplete: need 100ms prefix hints for 10M terms. API GET /suggest?q=. Storage trie in memory plus Kafka updates. Bottleneck rebuild; snippet queries sorted set.
output:
(integer) 1; top-5 'rust*' terms back, ranked
// <100ms prefix hints; no DB per keystroke

quiz.explain: Ranked prefix index serves instant hints.
options: SQL LIKE 'q%' query on every keystroke
Precomputed prefix index with ranked top-k
Full-text search engine query per keystroke
Rank all terms at read time by popularity
quiz.q: How do you serve typeahead fast?

takeaway: Precompute ranked prefixes at write time.

body_md: Notifications: requirements 50M pushes/day, dedupe, quiet hours. API enqueue event. Storage Kafka plus per-user queue. Bottleneck fan-out storms; snippet batches by user.
hook: Notification system: 50M pushes a day without spam.
output:
quiet hours: queued for later, no push now
else: batched + deduped send

options: Send each event immediately as it arrives
Broadcast to all devices on every account
Retry every failed send forever until delivered
Batch and dedupe per user, honor preferences
quiz.q: How do you avoid notification spam?

takeaway: Batch and dedupe per user with backoff.

body_md: Ride-hailing match: need nearby drivers <500ms, surge. API request ride, update location. Storage geo index Redis GEOADD, trips in Postgres. Bottleneck geo query; snippet searches radius.
code:
GEOADD drivers 77.2 28.6 driver:9
GEORADIUS drivers 77.2 28.6 3 km
hook: Ride matching: find the nearest driver in 500ms.
output:
(integer) 1 (driver indexed); query returns driver ids within 3 km
// then rank by ETA + surge

quiz.explain: Geospatial index prunes candidates before ranking.
options: Geo index for nearby drivers, then rank by ETA
Scan every active driver and sort by distance
Pick the straight-line closest driver only
Query trips in Postgres by city on each request
quiz.q: How do you match riders fast?

takeaway: Geo-query then rank by ETA and surge.

body_md: Video pipeline: requirements 4K upload, transcode, HLS. API upload, webhook done. Storage S3 raw plus CDN segments. Bottleneck transcode; snippet enqueues job.
code:
# enqueue transcode
ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -map 0 -c:v libx264 out.m3u8
hook: Video pipeline: upload once, play everywhere.
output:
job enqueued; worker transcodes to HLS segments on CDN
// upload returns at once; playback adapts per device

quiz.explain: Async workers plus CDN decouple upload from playback.
options: Async transcode to HLS segments served by a CDN
Transcode inside the upload request, then save
Stream the original uploaded file to every viewer
Serve segments straight from the origin bucket
quiz.q: How do you serve video at scale?

takeaway: Async transcode, segment, cache at edge.

body_md: E-commerce checkout: requirements cart, pay once, inventory. API reserve, charge idempotent, confirm. Storage orders Postgres, stock Redis decrement. Bottleneck oversell; snippet uses saga.
code:
POST /pay
Idempotency-Key: abc
-- reserve stock, charge, confirm
hook: Checkout design: never sell the last shirt twice.
output:
1st POST -> 200 charged; retry with key abc -> same stored result
// reserve -> charge -> confirm saga; no oversell

quiz.explain: Reserve plus idempotent charge plus confirm avoids double-sell.
options: Charge first, then check stock and refund if out
Check stock on page load and trust it at checkout
Reserve stock, charge idempotently, then confirm
Decrement stock only after the order ships

trap: No fencing letting two checkouts win.

body_md: Metrics pipeline: need 1M points/sec ingest, 7-day queries. API write batch, query range. Storage Kafka to ClickHouse downsampled. Bottleneck cardinality; snippet batches writes.
hook: Metrics pipeline: a million points a second, queryable.
output:
1000-pt batches -> AggregatingMergeTree, downsampled by age
// 1M pts/s ingest with fast 7-day range queries

quiz.explain: Batch plus columnar plus downsampling tames volume.
options: Batch writes into columnar store, downsample old
Insert one row per data point as it arrives
Keep full-resolution data forever for accuracy
Send every point in its own HTTP request to the DB
quiz.q: How do you ingest metrics cheaply?
